quick: One capsule (e.g., OM-85 7 mg) once daily, typically 10 days/month for 3 months
Take on an empty stomach before breakfast
summary: Bacterial lysates (e.g., OM-85, polyvalent mechanical/chemical lysates) are immunostimulants prepared from inactivated respiratory-pathogen bacteria, used to reduce the frequency of recurrent respiratory tract infections. They are not FDA-approved; information derives from EMA/national SmPC and clinical literature. Taken in monthly cycles, usually on an empty stomach.
indications: Prevention of recurrent respiratory tract infections (adjuvant to standard treatment)
Reduction in frequency of recurrent acute bronchitis and upper respiratory infections
Adjunctive immunoprophylaxis in patients prone to recurrent ear, nose and throat or bronchial infections

dosage.d: One 7 mg capsule once daily on an empty stomach
dosage.n: 10 consecutive days per month for 3 consecutive months (typical OM-85 course)
Until symptoms resolve (minimum ~10 days), alongside standard therapy

dosage.d: One 3.5 mg pediatric capsule/sachet once daily
dosage.n: 10 days/month for 3 months; follow local label

admin: Swallow the capsule whole on an empty stomach, before breakfast
For young children, the capsule contents may be dispersed in a drink per the product instructions
Follow the monthly cyclic schedule (commonly 10 days on per month for 3 months)
Continue any prescribed antibiotic or standard therapy during acute infections
moa: Standardized lysate of inactivated respiratory bacteria acts as an immunomodulator: it stimulates gut-associated and systemic immune responses, enhancing macrophage and dendritic-cell activity, increasing secretory IgA, and modulating T-cell responses. This is thought to prime mucosal defenses and reduce the frequency and severity of respiratory infections.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to the bacterial lysate or any excipient

preg: Safety during pregnancy has not been established; use is generally not recommended unless clearly necessary.
lact: It is not known whether components pass into breast milk; use during breastfeeding is not recommended.
renal: No specific dose adjustment has been established for renal impairment.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment has been established for hepatic impairment.

moderate: Immunosuppressant drugs - may reduce the immunostimulant effect
interactions.food: Take on an empty stomach; food may reduce absorption/effect.

emergency: Severe allergic reaction / anaphylaxis (swelling, breathing difficulty)

monitoring: Frequency and severity of respiratory tract infections over the course
counsel: Take on an empty stomach, following the monthly cycle your doctor prescribes
This medicine helps prevent infections but does not replace antibiotics for an active infection
Stop and seek care if you develop a rash, swelling or breathing difficulty
Benefit is seen as fewer infections over months, not immediate symptom relief
pk: Immunomodulatory effect develops over weeks of cyclic dosing
Not characterized (acts via mucosal/systemic immune priming)
Not applicable (not a conventional small molecule)
Effect may persist for months after a treatment course
Store below 25 C, protected from moisture
pearls: NOTE: Not FDA-approved; data based on EMA/national SmPC (e.g., OM-85 Broncho-Vaxom/Bronchomunal) and clinical trials, not a US FDA label
Typical schedule is 10 days per month for 3 consecutive months
Best used as adjunctive prophylaxis in recurrent respiratory infections, not to treat acute bacterial infection alone
Marketed products differ (mechanical vs chemical lysates); follow the specific product label
missed: Take the missed dose when remembered on a treatment day; if it is nearly time for the next day's dose, skip it and continue the schedule. Do not take two doses at once.
overdose: No specific antidote; overdose is unlikely to cause serious toxicity. Manage any gastrointestinal or allergic symptoms supportively.
